notes: The hourly pulse scans the worn jade ring and spiked armor; manual do_tick reaches the successful 5% armor branch, stores the player ID, and the next mobile pulse pursues Skarash across rooms. C's self-addressed do_tell is rejected silently; no player-facing tell is invented. R1/R3/R5e/R5h.

The deterministic pulse crosses the hourly callback with both hunted objects worn and Skarash available; the subsequent manual tick and pursuit make callback or draw-order regressions fail the proof. R3/R5e/R5h.
C wear-slot, hunted-item table, and character_list order decide which hunter claims each successful draw; each worn match consumes one C number(0,100) draw. R3/R5e/R5h.
Fighting, sleeping, charmed, and already-hunting candidates are skipped after the item chance draw, matching the source order. R3/R5e/R5h.
The scan visits only CON_PLAYING descriptor bodies in newest-first descriptor_list order, including a switched body. R5e/R5h.
Hunt state stores the positive player ID, resolves it only through a playing descriptor, preserves it when linkless, and pursues the resolved player when present. R1/R5e/R5h.
